summary.intent: Debug desktop E2E test failures in CI after merging IPNS signed record storage changes, identify root cause, and fix it.
summary.outcome: Identified two bugs: (1) `parseCachedRecord` in the API was returning the sequence number from inside the record bytes (client-submitted, could be 0) instead of the authoritative DB column value, causing stale sequence numbers to be returned on resolve; (2) the Rust FUSE `PublishCoordinator` cache was never seeded from the pre-populate resolve at mount time. Both fixes were applied and verified by running the full local desktop E2E suite (5/5 tests passing, no conflicts).

repo: The desktop client publishes root folder IPNS at sequence 0 (record bytes), but upsertFolderIpns always increments the DB column to 1 — so the DB sequence and the embedded record sequence are intentionally out of sync by 1 after init.
Desktop E2E only runs on main pushes, not on PR branches, which means regressions can slip through PR CI.
The FUSE `PublishCoordinator` seq_cache is the authoritative local source for expected sequence numbers during background metadata publishes; if empty, it re-resolves from the API.

vault.service.ts initVault creates a FolderIpns placeholder at seq 0; the actual first publish from the desktop increments it to 1 before vault/init is called, so the duplicate key catch in vault.service.ts only updates isRoot.
The desktop init flow order: IPNS publish (seq 0 record → DB seq 1) → /vault/init (duplicate key → just sets isRoot) → FUSE mount.
CI uses `vite preview --port 1420` to serve the frontend so the Tauri webview can complete the dev-key auth flow in headless mode.

code.finding: parseCachedRecord was extracting sequenceNumber from the signedRecord bytes (client-submitted value, e.g. 0) rather than using cached.sequenceNumber (the authoritative DB column, e.g. 1). Fixed to use the DB column.

PublishCoordinator was initialized with an empty seq_cache and never seeded from the pre-populate IPNS resolve responses at mount time, causing first background publishes to use expected_sequence_number=0.

resolve_sequence checks cache first, then resolves from API; if cache is empty and API returns seq 0 (due to parseCachedRecord bug), the publish sends expected=0 but server has 1 → 409 → persistent conflict.

initVault creates FolderIpns with sequenceNumber '0' as a placeholder; if the desktop IPNS publish already ran (which it does first), the save() hits duplicate key and only updates isRoot — sequence is preserved at 1.
Desktop publishes root folder IPNS at sequence 0 with no expectedSequenceNumber (None), which is why record bytes always contain sequence=0 while the DB stores sequence=1.

workflow: Before concluding a test failure is a pre-existing flaky issue, check the last N CI runs — 10 consecutive passes is strong evidence of a regression.
When a new API code path parses stored bytes, verify that the bytes' embedded values are not used as authoritative sources when a separate DB column tracks the canonical value.
Local desktop E2E reproduction requires: Docker stack, API running with .env, vite preview on port 1420, and the Rust binary built with FUSE feature — all must be up before running the test script.
1Password SSH signing agent can block automated git commits; keep commits manual or ensure the signing agent is running before automation attempts to commit.

friction: 1Password SSH signing agent blocked automated git commit twice, requiring manual user intervention to commit.
No .env file existed locally for the API — had to reconstruct from .env.example with a placeholder JWT_SECRET.
Desktop Rust binary requires a full Tauri build (slow) and a running vite preview server to complete dev-key auth — not obvious from reading the test script alone.
Desktop E2E only runs on main, not PRs, so the regression wasn't caught before merge.
Significant time spent ruling out non-causes (publicKey validation, delegated routing mock, vault init sequence) before identifying parseCachedRecord as the root cause.
open_items: The desktop client publishes root folder IPNS with sequence=0 in record bytes while the server stores sequence=1 — this fundamental mismatch is papered over by the fix but the client could be updated to publish at the correct sequence.
Subfolder IPNS sequence seeding was added to the coordinator but the root cause fix on the API side means it may not be strictly necessary — the Rust-side fix is defense-in-depth.
Consider running a subset of desktop E2E (or at least a smoke test) on PR branches to catch regressions before merge.
The mock IPNS routing service showed as 'unhealthy' locally — worth investigating whether the mock is reliable in CI.
